title: Horn of a bull, hoof of a horse, smile of a Saxon
html_source:
Horn of a bull = Witty, sharp

hoof of a horse = quick, agile

smile of a Saxon = charming, attracive

Overall message? He’s saying he’s crafty.

It’s a French expression listing the things one shouldn’t trust.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: An Irish proverb, “Beware the horns of a bull, the heels of a horse, and the smile of an Englishman.”
